courseDesc: Learn how scams work, recognize imposter scams, understand their dangers, and protect yourself from fraud.

What Are Scams?.question: What is a scam?
choices: A trick designed to deceive someone for personal gain

What Are Scams?.question: What is the main purpose of a scam?
choices: To benefit the scammer through money, information, or other rewards

What Are Scams?.question: Who is responsible for creating scams?
choices: People or groups trying to deceive others for personal gain

What Are Scams?.question: What might a scammer want from a victim?
Where can scams happen?
choices: Anywhere, including online and in person

What Are Scams?.question: When can someone become a target of a scam?
Which of these is an example of a scam?
choices: A store offering a real discount
Someone pretending to be from your bank to steal your password

What Are Scams?.question: What does a scammer usually try to make a victim do?
choices: Trust them and take an action that benefits the scammer

What Are Scams?.question: Are all scams committed by people who are physically nearby?
choices: No, scammers can operate from anywhere in the world

What Are Scams?.question: What is the difference between a scam and an honest mistake?
choices: A scam involves deliberate deception to gain something
A scam always involves stealing cash
An honest mistake is always illegal

What Are Scams?.question: Why might scammers pretend to be someone else?
choices: To make people trust them more easily

What Are Scams?.question: Which of these is a common characteristic of a scam?
choices: Encouraging you to take your time

What Are Scams?.question: Can a scammer be someone pretending to represent a legitimate organization?
choices: Only if the organization is a bank
Yes, scammers frequently impersonate trusted organizations

What Are Scams?.question: What does financial fraud involve?
choices: Deceiving someone to obtain money or financial benefits

What Are Scams?.question: Which statement about scams is TRUE?
choices: Scams only happen to wealthy people
Anyone can become a target of a scam

What Are Scams?.question: In your own words, explain what a scam is and what a scammer wants.
Who can become a victim of a scam, and where can scams happen?

How Imposter Scams Work.question: What is an imposter scam?
choices: A scam in which someone pretends to be a trusted person or organization
A scam involving only stolen credit cards

How Imposter Scams Work.question: Why do scammers impersonate trusted people or organizations?
choices: To make their identities easier to verify
To gain someone's trust and make their lies believable

How Imposter Scams Work.question: Which of these is commonly impersonated by scammers?
Someone calls claiming to be from the IRS and says you will be arrested unless you pay immediately. What type of scam is this?
A person receives an email claiming their computer has a virus and that a fake technician can fix it for a fee. What type of scam is this?
Why are imposter scams particularly effective?
choices: They exploit people's trust in familiar people and organizations
They only target people who have never used computers

How Imposter Scams Work.question: According to the FTC's 2024 fraud data, which was the most commonly reported fraud category?
Approximately how many imposter scam reports did the FTC receive in 2024?
Approximately how much money did Americans report losing to imposter scams in 2024?
What is a government imposter scam?
choices: A scammer pretending to represent a government agency
A government employee explaining tax rules

How Imposter Scams Work.question: What is a business imposter scam?
choices: A company opening a new location
A business offering a legitimate refund
A scammer pretending to represent a legitimate company
A customer writing a negative review

How Imposter Scams Work.question: You receive a call from someone claiming to be your bank. They say your account is compromised and request your password. What should you suspect?
Why might a scammer pretend to be a police officer?
choices: To intimidate someone into following their demands
To help someone file a report

How Imposter Scams Work.question: What is a family emergency imposter scam?
choices: A relative asking for normal advice
Someone pretending to be a relative in trouble and demanding money
A family member scheduling a visit

How Imposter Scams Work.question: A stranger claims to be your grandchild and says they urgently need money for bail. What should you do?
choices: Contact your grandchild or another trusted family member through a known number

How Imposter Scams Work.question: What is a romance scam?
choices: A scam involving fake concert tickets
A scammer pretending to have romantic feelings to manipulate someone into sending money

How Imposter Scams Work.question: Why do scammers sometimes impersonate technology support employees?
choices: People may trust experts to help with technical problems
Technology employees can legally request all passwords
They want to teach people programming
They are required to collect gift cards

How Imposter Scams Work.question: What is a common warning sign of a fake government official?
choices: They provide a publicly listed office number
They threaten immediate arrest unless you pay using an unusual method
They tell you to verify information independently
They send you to an official government website

How Imposter Scams Work.question: Why might a scammer use the name or logo of a famous company?
choices: To make a fraudulent message appear legitimate

How Imposter Scams Work.question: Which statement about caller ID is TRUE?
choices: Caller ID always identifies the real caller
Government agencies cannot be impersonated by phone
A familiar phone number proves a call is legitimate
Scammers can manipulate caller ID to make calls appear trustworthy

How Imposter Scams Work.question: Explain how an imposter scam works, including who the scammer pretends to be and what they want.
Name three organizations or people scammers commonly impersonate.

The Consequences of Scams.question: What is one possible financial consequence of falling for a scam?
How can a scam affect someone's personal information?
choices: It can expose sensitive information that scammers may misuse
It makes all accounts more secure

The Consequences of Scams.question: What is identity theft?
choices: Using another person's personal information without permission, often for fraud
Creating a new social media account

The Consequences of Scams.question: Which of these could happen after identity theft?
How might being scammed affect someone's mental or emotional well-being?
choices: It may cause stress, embarrassment, anxiety, or loss of trust
It always makes them more confident
It has no possible emotional impact

The Consequences of Scams.question: Why should people avoid blaming scam victims?
choices: Scams only target people who make mistakes
Scammers deliberately manipulate people, and anyone can be targeted
Victims are always responsible for the crime

The Consequences of Scams.question: Why are scams a concern for society, not just individual victims?
choices: They are limited to online shopping
They can damage trust, harm businesses, and impose costs on communities

The Consequences of Scams.question: How might a scam affect a victim's family?
choices: It can never affect anyone besides the victim
It may reduce shared savings or create emotional and financial stress

The Consequences of Scams.question: Why might someone hesitate to report a scam?
choices: They feel embarrassed or fear being judged
They are legally forbidden to report it
Reporting automatically makes them a criminal

The Consequences of Scams.question: Does losing money to a scam mean the victim is unintelligent?
choices: No, scammers use deliberate psychological manipulation and deception
Only if the scam happens online
Only if the victim is young

The Consequences of Scams.question: Why should you care about scams even if you have never been targeted?
choices: Scams are becoming impossible to detect
Only your family can be affected
You or someone you know could become a target in the future

The Consequences of Scams.question: What can happen when scammers obtain someone's login credentials?
choices: The account becomes impossible to access
The account automatically receives extra security
The victim gets a free subscription
Scammers may access accounts and steal information or money

The Consequences of Scams.question: Why can scams be especially damaging when victims are pressured to act quickly?
choices: They may make decisions without checking whether the situation is real
They have more time to investigate

The Consequences of Scams.question: Explain three different ways a scam can harm someone.
Why is it important to understand scams even if you have never personally experienced one?

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What is a common sign of a suspicious email?
choices: A message from a known contact about a normal topic
Unexpected requests for sensitive information or urgent payments
A receipt for a purchase you made

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: You receive a text saying your package cannot be delivered until you pay a small unexpected fee through a link. What should you do?
choices: Click the link and enter your card information
Verify the delivery directly through the carrier's official website or app
Forward the message to everyone you know

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What is a common warning sign of a fake tech support scam?
choices: An unexpected warning tells you to call a number or grant remote computer access
Your computer receives a normal software update
You contact the manufacturer's official support service

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What is phishing?
choices: A scam that uses deceptive messages or websites to steal information

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What is spoofing?
choices: Making a communication appear to come from a different or trusted source

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: Which of these is a suspicious payment request?
choices: Paying a normal bill through an official website
Paying a known merchant with a credit card
Being told to pay a government fine with gift cards

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: A stranger offers you a guaranteed investment return with no risk. What should you think?
choices: It is a major warning sign because legitimate investments carry risk
It is guaranteed to be legitimate
You should invest all your savings
You should share your bank password

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: Which statement about professional-looking scam messages is TRUE?
choices: Professional design proves a message is genuine
Scam messages can look convincing and contain correct spelling and logos
Only poorly written messages are scams

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: Why is an unexpected attachment in an email potentially dangerous?
choices: It may contain malware or lead to a fraudulent website

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What should you do when a message says you have won a prize you never entered to win?
choices: Treat it as suspicious, especially if it demands a fee or personal information

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What should you do if an online romantic partner suddenly asks for emergency money?
choices: Be cautious, independently verify their identity, and do not send money to someone you have not reliably verified

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What is the safest response to a suspicious message asking for your Social Security number?
choices: Do not provide it and independently verify the request
Send it to prove your identity
Post it in a public comment
Send it through an unverified link

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: What should you do if someone pressures you to make an immediate financial decision?
choices: Pause and independently verify the request before doing anything

Warning Signs and Scenarios.question: A caller says they are from the police and demands gift cards to prevent your arrest. Identify at least two warning signs.
Explain why a professional-looking email or a familiar phone number does not necessarily mean a communication is legitimate.

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do if a caller claims to be from your bank and asks for your password?
choices: Transfer your money to their account
End the call and contact your bank using a trusted number

Protecting Yourself.question: What is one way to check whether a suspicious phone call is genuine?
choices: Ask the caller to repeat their threats
Hang up and independently contact the organization through its official contact information
Give the caller your personal details

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do before clicking a link in an unexpected message?
choices: Check the sender and destination carefully, and access the organization independently if needed

Protecting Yourself.question: Which of these is a good way to protect your online accounts?
choices: Use strong unique passwords and enable multifactor authentication
Write your passwords in public posts

Protecting Yourself.question: What is multifactor authentication?
choices: Sharing your account with several people
Using an additional verification method beyond just your password

Protecting Yourself.question: Why should you avoid reusing passwords across different accounts?
choices: If one password is stolen, multiple accounts may become vulnerable
It makes your accounts easier to protect

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do if you accidentally click a suspicious link but do not enter any information?
choices: Close the page, avoid downloads or further interaction, and check your device if anything suspicious happened

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do if you have already shared your banking password with a suspected scammer?
choices: Immediately contact your bank through an official channel, change compromised credentials, and secure your account

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do if you have sent money to a scammer?
choices: Send more money to recover it
Wait for the scammer to return it
Contact your bank or payment provider immediately and ask whether the transaction can be stopped or reversed

Protecting Yourself.question: Where can people in the United States report scams?
choices: The Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do if you suspect someone is impersonating a government official?
choices: Stop communicating and verify the claim using the agency's independently obtained official contact information

Protecting Yourself.question: Why is it important to save messages and payment records after a scam?
choices: To make the scam spread faster
They may provide useful evidence when reporting the scam or contacting financial institutions
To guarantee that the money will be returned

Protecting Yourself.question: What should you do if a scammer threatens to release your personal information unless you pay?
choices: Do not panic or pay automatically; preserve evidence, secure accounts, and report the threat

Protecting Yourself.question: What is a credit freeze?
choices: A restriction that makes it harder for someone to open new credit accounts using your identity
A way to freeze your bank balance
A method of deleting your credit history
A way to stop all online purchases

Protecting Yourself.question: If you suspect identity theft, which action could help protect you?
choices: Consider placing a fraud alert or credit freeze with the credit bureaus
Share your Social Security number publicly
Close every online account without checking

Protecting Yourself.question: What is the safest way to verify whether a family member really needs emergency money?
choices: Trust any unfamiliar number claiming to be them
Contact the family member directly using a number you already know
Ask the caller for your banking password

Protecting Yourself.question: Why should you talk to someone you trust when you suspect a scam?
choices: They can automatically recover every lost dollar
They are legally required to pay you back
They can guarantee the caller's identity
A second opinion can help you recognize manipulation and avoid rushed decisions

Protecting Yourself.question: What is the most important thing to remember when dealing with a possible scam?
choices: Pause, verify independently, and never let pressure replace careful judgment
Always trust people who sound professional
Give information whenever someone asks confidently

Protecting Yourself.question: Describe at least three steps someone should take to protect themselves from scams.
Imagine you accidentally sent money to someone impersonating a government official. Explain what you should do next.
